clue.text: The places where convicts are intent going

definitions.text: The places where convicts are intent going

parts.words: The places where convicts are intent going
parts.note: read 'intent' as 'in tent': convicts housed under canvas, and the places where prisoners are kept

explanation.surface: A grim description of where determined convicts end up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'intent' into 'in tent': the convicts are going under canvas, as in a camp, and a jail holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: Camps for holding prisoners or captives, often under canvas, are places where convicts are kept.

clue.text: African up in space

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the word is written bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a Moor is a North African, one of the Berber-Arab peoples

explanation.surface: An African going up into outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MOOR around in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Room is space to move or fit things, as in 'no room to swing a cat'.

clue.text: Toss out the drunks!

indicators.note: 'out' here means the word toss is put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A landlord's cry to throw the drunks out of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of 'Toss'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sots are habitual drinkers, a dated word for drunkards.

clue.text: Ciphers and crosses follow child's game

explanation.surface: Codes and crosses feature in a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is noughts and crosses (tic-tac-toe): its first word, followed by 'and crosses', names the child's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is an old word for zero, the figure 0; and crosses follow this word in the name of the paper game tic-tac-toe.

clue.text: Strange laws on hand tools

indicators.note: strange signals that the word laws is turned into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Peculiar legislation concerning hand tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the letters of 'laws'.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a small pointed tool for piercing leather or wood, held in the hand.

clue.text: A contemporary gift

explanation.surface: Describing a modern-day gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Present as an adjective means existing now, current; as a noun it is something given, a gift.

clue.text: Be holding a tar baby

indicators.note: holding means the first word is wrapped around the second piece

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is the usual sailor abbreviation

explanation.surface: An instruction to cradle a tar baby, the sticky doll of folk tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts AB inside BE. A tar is a sailor, and AB stands for able-bodied seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Babe is an informal or poetic word for an infant.

clue.text: Fools in a theatre ends with a hit

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and the plural gives two of them
the second of the two fools, another ass
taken as written

indicators.note: ends means only the first and last letters of the word theatre are kept

explanation.surface: Idiots in a theatre close with a hit show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fools' gives two asses; then IN, A, and 'ends' gives TE, the first and last letters of 'theatre'. The hit is a murder, not a stage success.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is slang for a killing done to order, so to hit someone is to murder them.

clue.text: God it's sweet!

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight on tasting something sugary.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mars bar is a well-known chocolate bar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is the Roman war deity, and a Mars bar is a chocolate confection.

clue.text: He made a bluebird to perform for sir Donald!

definitions.text: He made a bluebird to perform for sir Donald!

indicators.note: perform here asks the letters of 'a bluebird to' to act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Praise for the man who constructed Bluebird so it could race for Sir Donald Campbell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perform' rearranges the eleven letters of 'a bluebird to'. Sir Donald Campbell set water speed records in boats called Bluebird, so the whole clue describes such a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who constructs vessels for the water built Campbell's record-breaking Bluebird hydroplanes.

clue.text: The middle age of a goddess

indicators.note: the middle of the three-letter word The is its central letter

parts.note: an age is an era, a long period of history

explanation.surface: A goddess in middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The middle' gives H, the centre letter of 'The'; then ERA for 'age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera is the Greek queen of the deities, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: He mates more than most

parts.note: sounds like a ladies' man, but mating here is checkmating a king on the board

explanation.surface: A remark about a notably promiscuous man.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkmate is the winning move in the board game, so a keen competitor delivers mate often.

clue.text: Result in as an inevitable consequence of getting in late again

definitions.text: Result in as an inevitable consequence

indicators.note: again suggests the letters of 'in late' are made over once more, in a new order

explanation.surface: Being late again has unavoidable results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' rearranges the letters of 'in late'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or necessitate something as a necessary outcome.

clue.text: To sharpen pen is the best policy

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Advice that sharpening one's pen is wise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the proverb that this virtue 'is the best policy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says truthfulness is the wisest course, so the phrase stands for it.

clue.text: Reputedly a seed crop

explanation.surface: A crop said to come from a single seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reputedly' points to sound: to yield is to cede, which is said like 'seed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way is to cede, a word said like 'seed'; and a harvest is the produce a field gives.

clue.text: Apprehensive in a sense with the team

indicators.note: in places the team inside the word for sense

parts.note: nous is common sense, practical wit
XI, the Roman eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Nervous, along with the rest of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container. In cricket and football a team is an eleven, written XI in Roman numerals; nous is a British word for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious means worried or uneasy about what may come.

clue.text: Before, but one can also be in front

explanation.surface: Something comes earlier, and may also lead the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are the same word: earlier in time and leading in place.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means earlier or in advance, and also leading or forward of the rest.

clue.text: Choice of alternative potion

indicators.note: alternative signals another version of the word potion, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Selecting a different potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges the letters of 'potion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a selection one may make from several possibilities.

clue.text: Touch in a sense

parts.note: touch is one of the five faculties, and this answer is another of them, so it is touch 'in a sense'

explanation.surface: A remark that touch counts as one of the senses.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on 'in a sense': touch and the answer are both among the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses, alongside hearing, taste, smell and touch.

clue.text: Shot with a knife?

parts.note: a 'shot' is an attempt, and a knife thrust is another way to have one

explanation.surface: Was someone shot, or attacked with a blade?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' is an attempt, as in 'have a go'; the question mark asks for the knife sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is both an attempt at something and a thrust with a blade.

clue.text: Goes nuts over the floor

indicators.note: over means the word nuts is turned over and read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone goes crazy all over the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns 'nuts' backwards. 'floor' is a verb, to knock someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to knock them out or stagger them, as a blow or shock does.

clue.text: Jumpers who are surprisingly false

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the word false comes out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Sweaters that turn out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges 'false'. In Britain a jumper is a sweater, which is the false path; here jumpers are hopping insects.
explanation.definitionFit: These parasitic insects are famous for leaping great distances for their size.

clue.text: Is he more amorous in his first year at university?

definitions.text: Is he more amorous in his first year at university?

parts.words: Is he more amorous in his first year at university?
parts.note: 'fresh' can mean forward or cheeky with the opposite sex, and a first-year student is also called by the comparative of that word

explanation.surface: A question about whether a new undergraduate is especially amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a first-year student is a fresher; 'fresh' also means forward in a flirtatious way, so 'more fresh' fits 'more amorous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A British first-year student is so called, and the same word is the comparative of 'fresh', meaning cheeky.

clue.text: Leak classified intelligence finally

parts.note: classified information is secret

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word intelligence is used

explanation.surface: A spy leaks classified intelligence at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E, the last letter of 'intelligence'. 'Leak' is to ooze, not to reveal.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is to discharge a fluid, as glands ooze it out.

clue.text: Hohead for a road to cut the crown from a tree

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Hohead for a road to cut the crown from a tree': 'Hohead' is not a word; the wordplay POLL + A + RD needs 'Head', and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Hohead for a road to cut the crown from a tree

clue.text: Dottier course of action here in Michigan

indicators.note: course of action suggests the letters of Dottier are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A dottier course of action is taken in Michigan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course of action' rearranges the letters of 'Dottier'.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the largest city in the US state of Michigan, the Motor City.

clue.text: Sadly it's a girl, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a lass is a girl, chiefly in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: Disappointment at the birth of a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says 'a lass' (a girl) is said like the answer, an expression of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of sorrow, used like 'unfortunately'.

clue.text: Somewhat tart but mostly placid

indicators.note: mostly means most of the letters of placid are kept, a run held within it

explanation.surface: Somewhat sharp, but generally calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' keeps the last four letters of 'placid'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective means sour or sharp-tasting, like vinegar.

clue.text: Room to put one's arms up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: arms are weapons such as guns

explanation.surface: A room where one is told to raise one's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GUNS around in this down light. A snug is a small, cosy room in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A snug is a small private bar-room in a pub, or any cosy little room.

clue.text: Information from all points of the globe

parts.note: the first compass point used is north, abbreviated N
the second compass point is east, abbreviated E
the third compass point is west, abbreviated W
the last compass point is south, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: Reports gathered from every corner of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The four points of the compass, read north, east, west, south, give the letters in order; 'from all points' also hints that information arrives from everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: News is fresh information about recent events.

clue.text: Love to oil up a dish of meat

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word oil is read bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A cook lovingly oiling a meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns 'oil' around in this down light, after O for love (nil in tennis).
explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a Spanish or Portuguese stew of meat and vegetables, a hotchpotch.

clue.text: Fungus the singer put in front of French woman

indicators.note: put in front of places the singer before the French woman in the answer

parts.note: a chanter is one who sings or chants
elle is French for she, standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A fungus placed before a French lady by a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in front of' orders the charade: the singer comes first. 'Fungus' at the start is the definition, not part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The chanterelle is an edible, apricot-coloured woodland mushroom.

clue.text: Was it way out, or was it to leave

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether something was a way out or a departure.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a door or route out; to exit is to depart.

clue.text: Advance of prisoners go amok

indicators.note: running amok means going wild, so the letters of prisoners go are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Prisoners run riot, and the authorities advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amok' rearranges the letters of 'prisoners go'.
explanation.definitionFit: Progression is forward movement or advancement from one stage to the next.
